summary:
Lanes.partition (FS.GG.Coord.Core) groups open items into lanes: two items join iff they are in the same repository and TouchSet.conflicts finds an overlapping token pair, the same predicate the batch scheduler reserves against. Lanes are the transitive closure (union-find), so A-B and B-C put A and C in one lane. Pairs joined only by a generated, CI-gated path (ADR-0044) do not glue.

Lanes.glue ranks a lane's tokens by SplitsInto: how many lanes the lane would split into if that token were removed. It is hypothetical and changes nothing. Narrowing a real Paths declaration is a judgement for the issue owner (the lane-steward skill), because a touch-set narrowed wrongly lets batch hand held files to another worker.

Generic technique: union-find (ADR-0098 harvest 19). A DSM or graph-partitioning kernel was judged not worth a library entry. ADR-0098 §11 tranche 2 (FS-GG/.github#5245) lists this record; the generic technique is a pack entry, the FS-GG instance stays here (§10).
title: Lane partition and cut analysis: union-find lanes and Lanes.glue token ranking
